data.narrative:
Code Metal, a Series B defense and security company founded by Peter Morales and Alex Showalter-Bucher, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 10 firms (2 public, 8 private) operating in the same sector and stage. The peer set includes Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Defense Unicorns, Heven AeroTech, and TurbineOne, with valuations ranging from $300M to $3.0B.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, grounding on Code Metal's last post-money valuation of $1.2B, applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement to next-stage funding, yielding $2.4B. Peer-median analysis across the five same-sector, same-stage comparables produces a $1.0B implied value, with the peer distribution spanning $300M to $3.0B.

Triangulation of these methods produces a valuation range of $850M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.7B. Code Metal's current $1.25B valuation sits in the lower-middle portion of this range. Key uncertainties include dispersion within the peer set—the $3.0B high outlier versus the $300M minimum—and the appropriateness of applying a uniform 1.9x step-up multiplier absent visibility into Code Metal's growth metrics relative to cohort benchmarks. Revenue trajectory and customer concentration remain material to narrowing this band.
